figures.caption: Figure 1: A fragment of an OOMRAM lattice showing core (blue), single-adaptor (SA, green), multiple-adaptor (MA, orange), and optional (gray, dashed) nodes. Parent-child relationships are indicated by arrows.

Figure 2: Neuro-symbolic agent workflow. The Navigator selects the next discriminant node. The Interpreter (LLM) proposes a set of child IDs based on the project vision. The symbolic Validator checks structural constraints; if a violation occurs (red dashed loop), the Interpreter revises its proposal. Accepted selections (green arrow) are sent to the Scribe, which compiles the final specification. The ⟨T, I, F ⟩ label indicates where threevalued discretion scoring is applied at the Validator output before the rejection branch.
Table 2: Three-valued T/I/F classification scores per requirement node type (counts and row percentages, all runs pooled).
Table 5: Validator ablation: comparison of full system (with Validator) versus counterfactual baseline (without Validator) across 37 visions.

Table 6: Comparison of our neuro-symbolic system against four unguarded LLM strategies, all evaluated on the same 37 visions using Llama 3.1. Structural Falsity is the % of visions with ≥ 1 uncorrected constraint violation.
Table 7: Per-family three-valued T/I/F totals and indeterminacy proportion ρI = I/(T + I + F ), sorted descending.
Table 3: Annotated decision trace for vision er_small_biz (eRecord Keeping family, 39 requirements selected from 57 nodes, 101 LLM calls).
